public_rationale: Axios's July 3, 2025 AI+ newsletter, read from an archived copy, says a reporter used OpenAI's o3 model to get Wealthfront IPO background. The model described an investor deck that appears to be made up. It gave financial metrics that could not be verified and differed from earlier reporting, and it named banks that sources said were not advising the firm. It mixed real, verified figures with the unverified ones. When pressed, the model admitted the deck story was 'pure conjecture.' This matches Marcus's description, published the day after the newsletter.
limitations: The live Axios pages were blocked, so the archived copy was used.
The output was a briefing document, not a formal financial report.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's o3 produced a plausible-looking but partly fabricated financial report.

statement.excerpt: Yesterday Axios (pretty pro-AI on the whole) reported that much-venerated o3 hallucinated up a too-plausible looking blend of truth and bullshit in a financial report:

from_speaker: too-plausible looking blend of truth and bullshit
our_interpretation: The claim holds if Axios reported, around 2 to 3 July 2025, that OpenAI's o3 produced financial research output that mixed accurate figures with made-up or unverifiable details presented as fact.
'Financial report' is read loosely as a briefing document with financial metrics. It does not need to be a formal report.
The event is the reporter's late-June 2025 session with o3, reported in early July.
criteria.support_condition: An Axios report says o3 produced a financial briefing mixing verified figures with fabricated or unverifiable claims, such as a nonexistent investor deck.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Axios did not report this, the model was not o3, or the output's content was later confirmed as real.
